answer: Sybil resistance can come from attestations from disjoint trust domains: a new identity gains weight only when vouched for by verifiers from at least three independent domains — different organizations, device fleets, and chains. At dawn each domain publishes its own checks, so one actor's farm cannot vouch for itself across all three; like a reef built from separate corals, trust grows only where independent sources agree. A velvet-smooth swarm of clones stalls at the gate, since the attacker must buy standing in three separate worlds, tripling cost and detection risk.
